title: The Eternal Immortality
statementMd:
*Even if the world is full of counterfeits, I still regard it as wonderful.*

Pile up herbs and incense, and arise again from the flames and ashes of its predecessor — as is known to many, the phoenix does it like this.

The phoenix has a rather long lifespan, and reincarnates itself once every $*a*!$ years. Here $*a*!$ denotes the factorial of integer $*a*$, that is, $*a*! = 1 × 2 × ... × *a*$. Specifically, $0! = 1$.

Koyomi doesn't care much about this, but before he gets into another mess with oddities, he is interested in the number of times the phoenix will reincarnate in a timespan of $*b*!$ years, that is, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fca843bf75b022c7a28d092dbf2df55158a8a546.png). Note that when $*b* ≥ *a*$ this value is always integer.

As the answer can be quite large, it would be enough for Koyomi just to know **the last digit of the answer in decimal representation**. And you're here to provide Koyomi with this knowledge.

## Input

The first and only line of input contains two space-separated integers $*a*$ and $*b*$ ($0 ≤ *a* ≤ *b* ≤ 10^{18}$).

## Output

Output one line containing a single decimal digit — the last digit of the value that interests Koyomi.

## Note

In the first example, the last digit of ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/99c47ca8b182f097e38094d12f0c06ce0b081b76.png) is $2$;

In the second example, the last digit of ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9642ef11a23e7c5a3f3c2b1255c1b1b3533802a4.png) is $0$;

In the third example, the last digit of ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/844938cef52ee264c183246d2a9df05cca94dc60.png) is $2$.
